types.name: LitVertex
types.doc:
tangent.w is the bitangent handedness, +1 or -1. Every consumer must build
the bitangent as cross(normal, tangent.xyz) * tangent.w: a mirrored UV shell
(the other half of a symmetric character, a flipped decal sheet) carries the
opposite handedness from its twin, and a fixed cross(N, T) lit those shells
as if their normal map's green channel were inverted.

texCoord1 is the lightmap/second channel. It is packed and serialized even
when the source has one UV set (it then mirrors texCoord), because the
vertex layout is shared across every pipeline: an attribute that appears
only sometimes would shift every later attribute's shader location.

types.name: FVertexLayouts
types.doc:
The single source of truth for the lit/skinned vertex input. Every pipeline
that draws a GPUMesh declares its layout through these rather than spelling
the attributes out: VertexLayout derives both the byte offsets and (on
Vulkan/Metal) the shader attribute locations from declaration order, so one
copy that drifts from the struct above silently feeds every later attribute
the wrong bytes.

types.name: MorphTarget
types.doc:

members.name: TargetMaxDelta

vertices back: the base box grown by sum(|weight| * the target's largest

members.name: GetId
members.doc:
Process-unique and monotonic. Anything that caches on mesh identity has
to key on this rather than the pointer: a streaming unload hands the
freed address straight back to whatever loads next, so two different
meshes can share an address and compare equal.

members.name: GetVertexBuffer
members.doc:
The whole-mesh accessors resolve through the resident chain exactly like
the per-LOD ones below. Returning the raw base buffers meant a
mesh-streaming eviction of LOD0 handed null to every draw site still on
them (probe and planar captures, OIT, foliage, VSM casters, surface-cache
cards) — which is what kept r.MeshStreaming off by default.

members.name: GetBoneCount
members.doc:
Bone count = highest bone index referenced by the vertices + 1 (0 for
non-skinned). Lets a skinned mesh be drawn at bind pose by binding this
many identity matrices when no animation supplies skinning matrices.

members.name: AddLitLOD
members.signature: void AddLitLOD(const std::vector<LitVertex>& verts, const std::vector<uint32_t>& indices)
members.doc:
Discrete LOD chain. LOD 0 is the base buffers above; coarser
levels are appended by AddLitLOD with already-simplified geometry
(the simplifier lives in Game — Renderer just owns the buffers).
The per-LOD accessors clamp out-of-range indices to the coarsest
available level and fall back to the base mesh when no LODs exist,
so every draw site can ask for a LOD unconditionally.

members.name: AddSkinnedLOD
members.signature: void AddSkinnedLOD(const std::vector<SkinnedVertex>& verts, const std::vector<uint32_t>& indices)
members.doc:
Same chain for skinned meshes — the level buffers are format-agnostic,
only the upload stride differs, and every accessor below is shared.

members.name: SetLodErrors
members.doc:
Simplification error of each coarser level ([0] = LOD1) as a fraction
of the mesh's bounding-box diagonal, as the simplifier measured it.
Empty when nobody measured (primitives, pre-v15 cooks): the renderer
then picks levels by the global coverage boundaries.

members.name: EvictLitLOD
members.doc:
Evicting a level drops its GPU buffers; every accessor above falls back
to the finest RESIDENT level at or coarser than the request (and to the
coarsest overall when even that is gone), so legacy GetVertexBuffer()
callers keep drawing a consistent — merely coarser — mesh while LOD0 is
streamed out. Restore re-admits a level from CPU data (main thread).
The residency version bumps on every change: caches keyed on
(mesh, lod) snapshot buffers and must rebind when it moves.

members.signature: bool RestoreLitLODFilled(uint32_t lod, uint32_t vertexCount, uint32_t indexCount, EIndexFormat storedFormat, const FBufferFill& vertexFill, const FBufferFill& indexFill)

members.name: NoteDesiredLOD
members.doc:
Renderer-side desire note, read by the streaming manager: the finest
LOD any view asked for this frame. The parallel LOD resolve notes a
shared mesh from several workers at once, so the frame and the level
travel as one atomic word and a note only ever lowers the level within
its frame or starts a newer frame.

members.name: GetUvDensity
members.doc:
Mesh-local units one repeat of UV set 0 spans (sqrt of surface area over
UV area): the texel factor texture streaming scales by. Without it a
mesh was assumed to map its texture once across its largest extent, so
a tiled floor held mips it could never show and a mesh on an atlas
corner starved. 0 when the mesh has no usable UVs.

members.name: GetCPUPositions
members.doc:
CPU-side position + index data, kept alongside the GPU buffers so
gameplay subsystems (NavMesh baking, raycasts against arbitrary
meshes, future collision-shape generation) can read triangle data
without bouncing through a GPU readback. Populated by the Create*
factories. Empty for meshes that bypass those factories (rare —
currently every code path goes through them).

members.name: GetCPUSkinnedVertices

Empty for anything but a skinned mesh.

members.name: SetMorphTargets
members.signature: void SetMorphTargets(std::vector<MorphTarget> targets, const std::vector<LitVertex>& baseVertices)
members.doc:
Attach morph targets + snapshot the base vertices (Lit meshes only).
ApplyMorphWeights CPU-evaluates base + Σ w·delta and uploads the whole
vertex buffer; weights beyond the target count are ignored, missing
weights are 0.

members.name: SetSkinnedMorphTargets
members.doc:
Blend shapes on a skinned mesh: the deltas move the BIND pose and the
skin then deforms the result, the order every DCC and UE apply them in,
so a face shape rides the head bone instead of fighting it. CPU only:
the morph kernel writes the lit vertex layout.

members.name: ApplyMorphWeightsGPU
members.doc:
Queues the morph kernel for the next frame the renderer records: no
submit-and-wait and no vertex readback on the calling (game) thread. The
bounds become conservative and the CPU positions stay those of the last
CPU evaluation (the base pose until one ran), which only picking reads.

members.name: FlushPendingMorphDispatches
members.doc:
Records every queued morph dispatch into the open frame (render thread,
before the geometry passes); outside a frame they submit single-time.

members.name: SetMeshlets

Renderer just stores the data, mirroring the LOD split. The meshlet render
pass pools them into GPU buffers on residency — GPUMesh keeps only the
CPU copy.

types.name: GeometryPool
types.doc:
Shared geometry mega-buffer. One big vertex buffer + one big index
buffer that many meshes sub-allocate into; each allocation records its
(baseVertex, firstIndex, indexCount). Binding the pool ONCE then issuing a
single MultiDrawIndexedIndirect over N commands — each carrying its own
vertexOffset/firstIndex — is the batched GPU-driven draw: N meshes, one CPU
call. Replaces the per-mesh VB/IB bind+draw of the classic path.

Fixed capacity. Add() fails (valid=false) when no free range fits; callers
fall back to the per-mesh path for the overflow. Free() returns a slice's
ranges to first-fit free lists — the caller must know the GPU no longer
reads the slice, since the next admission may copy into it at once.

members.name: Create
members.signature: static Ref<GeometryPool> Create(uint32_t vertexCapacity, uint32_t indexCapacity, const std::string& debugName = "GeometryPool", EIndexFormat format = EIndexFormat::UInt32)
members.doc:
vertexCapacity/indexCapacity in elements (LitVertex / index). One pool
holds one index width: a draw binds the pool's buffer once, so a 16-bit
mesh copied byte for byte into a 32-bit pool would read as garbage.

members.signature: Alloc Add(const std::vector<LitVertex>& verts, const std::vector<uint32_t>& indices)
members.doc:
Upload a lit mesh's LOD-0 geometry into the pool. Returns the slice; on
overflow (or a 16-bit pool given an index above 65 535) returns
{valid=false} and uploads nothing.

members.name: AddFromBuffers
members.signature: Alloc AddFromBuffers(Ref<VertexBuffer> vb, Ref<IndexBuffer> ib, uint32_t vertexCount, uint32_t indexCount)
members.doc:
GPU→GPU residency path (live MDI): copy an existing mesh's buffers
into the pool without CPU vertex data (GPUMesh retains positions
only). vertexCount is in LitVertex elements, indexCount in indices.
The index buffer must have the pool's format; a mismatch is refused.

members.name: AddFromBuffersAsync
members.signature: Alloc AddFromBuffersAsync(Ref<VertexBuffer> vb, Ref<IndexBuffer> ib, uint32_t vertexCount, uint32_t indexCount, uint64_t& outTicket)
members.doc:
Async admission: reserves the slice immediately and submits the copy
fire-and-forget. outTicket = 0 means the backend ran it synchronously
(slice usable now); otherwise the slice must not be drawn from until
IDynamicRHI::IsAsyncUploadComplete(outTicket), and the caller keeps
vb/ib alive until then.

types.name: ELightIntensityUnits
types.doc:
Photometric intensity units for authored lights. Legacy keeps the historical
artist scale (raw intensity, range-window falloff). Every other unit converts
to shader radiance at the component -> renderer boundary and switches that
light to true inverse-square falloff:
Lumens  — luminous flux. Point: I = lm / 4pi. Spot: I = lm / (2pi(1-cos(outerAngle))),
outerAngle being the authored half-angle from the axis. Area: emitter
luminance L = lm / (pi * area * (twoSided ? 2 : 1)).
Candela — luminous intensity, used directly for punctual lights. Area: L = cd / area.
EV100   — exposure value at ISO 100; I (or L for area) = 2^(EV100 - 3).
Lux     — illuminance, DIRECTIONAL ONLY (the sun's ground-plane illuminance).
Cross-type fallback: Lux on a local light and Lumens/Candela/EV100 on a
directional light behave as Legacy.

members.name: KelvinToColor

only. kelvin <= 0 returns white (disabled). Valid range 1000-15000 K.

faces. IES profiles are not supported for area lights.

types.name: EShadingModel
types.doc:
Explicit surface shading model (G2). Values are the GBuffer wire IDs
(RT3.A bits 5..7) — renumbering breaks every already-rendered frame's
decode AND the CPU codec tests. 0 must remain DefaultLit: impostors,
decal-neutral writes and material-less draws all emit a zero alpha.

members.name: DefaultLit
members.doc: GGX; also "legacy auto" — derives Hair/Subsurface from the old scalar knobs

members.name: Unlit
members.doc: emissive passthrough, lighting skipped entirely

members.name: Subsurface
members.doc: Penner wrap-diffuse, strength in the custom lane, blurred by the SSS pass

members.name: ClearCoat
members.doc: second specular lobe (intensity/roughness keep their RT3 R/G lanes)

members.name: Hair
members.doc: Kajiya-Kay strands over the aniso tangent frame

members.name: TwoSidedFoliage
members.doc: adds albedo-tinted back-light transmission, strength in the custom lane

members.name: Cloth
members.doc: Charlie sheen lobe over the base diffuse — velvet, felt, brushed fabric

members.name: ThinTranslucent
members.doc:
Coloured glass: the surface TINTS what is behind it by Beer-Lambert
absorption instead of fading it. Transmission strength is the thickness.
NOTE: this fills the classic tier of RT3.A's surface code (0-6 plus this
one). Ids past it go through tier 7's escape, which names an extended
slot and moves that surface's payload to RT3.R/G — see FSurfaceCode.

members.name: Eye
members.doc:
The first EXTENDED model — it rides tier 7's escape, so RT3.R/G stop
being the clear coat's lanes and become a 16-bit record index into the
frame's surface-parameter buffer. Eye is the model that forced the
indirection: its defining input is a per-pixel iris normal, a float3
that no packed lane of any width was ever going to carry.

types.name: FEyeSurfaceParams
types.doc:
Eye's surface parameters. None of them reach the G-Buffer directly — the
renderer writes one FSurfaceRecord per drawn Eye material into the frame's
surface-parameter buffer and RT3 stores only that record's index, which is
what buys a lit pixel a whole struct instead of five bits.

members.name: IrisTint
members.doc:
Linear multiplier on the iris diffuse seen THROUGH the cornea. Kept
separate from base color so a single albedo texture can cover sclera
and iris while only the iris takes the tint.

members.name: CorneaIoR
members.doc:
Refractive index of the cornea (~1.376 in vivo). It sets both the
corneal Fresnel and how far the view ray bends before it reaches the
iris — the bend is the whole reason the iris needs its own normal.

members.name: IrisDepth
members.doc:
Anterior-chamber depth in world units: how far the iris sits behind the
corneal surface. 0 collapses the eye to a painted sphere, because
nothing is left for the refraction to travel through.

members.name: IrisConcavity
members.doc:
How far the iris has flattened out of the cornea's curvature, 0..1.
0 shades the iris with the corneal normal (indistinguishable from
DefaultLit); 1 faces it straight down the refracted ray.

members.name: GazeAxis
members.doc:
The eyeball's LOCAL pupil axis. Every field above is shared by every
draw of the material; this one is not, because the renderer transforms
it by each draw's own model matrix. That is the whole reason the record
is keyed per draw: two eyeballs on one material differ only by their
transform, and a material-keyed record made both eyes stare the same
way no matter where the heads were looking.

members.name: IrisConeDegrees
members.doc:
Half-angle of the iris disc about the gaze axis, in degrees, measured
from the eyeball's pivot. 0 disables the mask and the whole escaped
surface is iris — exactly what shipped before the mask existed, which
is why it is the default.

members.name: LimbalWidthDegrees
members.doc:
Angular width of the limbal transition in degrees: the iris fades out
across it and the ring darkens within it. Never applied at zero width —
a hard angular step aliases along the limbus at any resolution.

members.name: LimbalDarkening
members.doc:
Absorption in the limbal band, 0..1. 0 leaves the surface untouched, so
an eye authored before the ring existed is unmoved.

members.name: IrisRoughness
members.doc:
Roughness of the iris' OWN specular lobe, behind the cornea. 0 disables
it: the iris shipped diffuse-only, and a lobe that appeared by default
would move every existing eye.

members.name: CausticStrength
members.doc:
Light the corneal lens focuses onto the iris — the bright crescent
opposite a key light. 0 = off.

types.name: FWorldGridParams
types.doc:
The world-aligned procedural grid (UE's WorldGridMaterial). It is drawn by
the uber GBuffer shader from the pixel's world position and needs no texture
and no cooked graph shader, which is why it can be the material every mesh
without one falls back to. Base colour fills the cells; the shades multiply
it on the lines, so one value under 1 darkens the lines and one over 1
brightens them.

types.name: EMaterialBlendMode
types.doc:
How a TRANSLUCENT surface combines with the scene behind it. Opaque and
masked surfaces are expressed by opacity + alphaMasked and never reach
here. Values are serialized by index — append only.

members.name: Alpha
members.doc: src over dst — what every translucent did before this existed

members.name: Additive
members.doc: dst + src: fire, glows, holograms

members.name: Modulate
members.doc: dst * src: stained glass, smoked plastic

members.name: EyeParams
members.doc:
The last free bit, so Eye's five parameters share ONE override: they
are a single surface's description and are always authored together.

types.name: FMaterialIdentity
types.doc:
Process-unique material identity. Copies mint a FRESH id (a copy is a new
material object), assignment keeps the target's own — so an id never names
two live materials and, unlike the raw address it replaced as the DS-cache
key, is never reused after a delete (address reuse handed a new material
the previous occupant's cached descriptor set: wrong textures).

types.name: FMaterialTransparentDepth
types.doc:
Nesting depth of Material::FTransparentWriteScope. Copying a material never
copies an in-flight scope: the scope belongs to the operation running on the
ORIGINAL, and a render proxy that inherited a non-zero count would stop
recording override bits for the rest of its life.

types.name: FMaterialStateVersion
types.doc:
Count of surface changes on ONE material object, moved by every setter. The
render-proxy cache reuses last frame's snapshot while (identity, version)
still match, so a copy that carried the source's count would let a material
that was just overwritten by CopyFrom/ResetInPlace keep matching a snapshot
of what it used to be. Copying therefore never transfers it.

types.name: FMaterialState
types.doc:
Everything a material IS, kept apart from the object that carries the
reference count. Material derives from RefCounted, whose count must never be
copied — but the render proxy still snapshots a surface every frame and
Clone() still needs a field-wise duplicate. Holding the surface in a plainly
copyable base is what lets both of those exist without a hand-written
member list that silently skips the next field somebody adds.

members.name: m_metallic
members.doc: 0 = dielectric, 1 = metal

members.name: m_roughness
members.doc: 0 = smooth/mirror, 1 = rough/diffuse

members.name: m_ao
members.doc: Ambient occlusion (1 = no occlusion)

members.name: m_opacity
members.doc: 1 = opaque, < 1 = transparent

members.name: m_specularColor
members.doc: Legacy specular (for backward compatibility with non-PBR shaders)

members.name: m_metallicRoughnessTex
members.doc: Combined: R=metallic, G=roughness

members.name: m_opacityTex
members.doc: R = coverage (standalone cutout mask)

members.name: m_detailAlbedoTex
members.doc: overlay albedo

members.name: m_detailNormalTex
members.doc: overlay tangent-space normal

members.name: m_maskMapTex
members.doc: R=metallic, G=AO, B=detail mask, A=smoothness

members.name: m_heightTex
members.doc: R = height (0=surface, 1=deepest)

members.name: m_detailTiling
members.doc: UV multiplier for detail textures

members.name: m_detailAlbedoStrength
members.doc: 0..1 — blend amount over primary albedo

members.name: m_detailNormalStrength
members.doc: 0..1 — strength of detail normal influence

members.name: m_parallaxHeightScale
members.doc: POM displacement amount; 0.02-0.08 typical

members.name: m_displacementMagnitude
members.doc:
Meshlet-path geometric displacement from the height map, object-space
units; < 0 = not set here (an instance then takes its parent's; a root
reads 0 = off). No override bit is left in MaterialOverride, so the
sentinel is what carries "inherit".

members.name: m_displacementCenter
members.doc: height that stays put; < 0 = inherit / 0.5

members.name: m_clearCoatIntensity
members.doc: 0 = disabled, 1 = full lobe

members.name: m_clearCoatRoughness
members.doc: 0 = mirror coat (glossy), 1 = matte coat

members.name: m_anisotropy
members.doc: -1..1; 0 = isotropic GGX

members.name: m_subsurfaceStrength
members.doc: 0 = no SSS, 1 = max wrap

members.name: m_iridescenceIntensity
members.doc: 0 = no shift, 1 = full rainbow Fresnel

members.name: m_hair
members.doc: anisotropic Kajiya-Kay strand shading (hair/fur)

members.name: m_transmissionStrength
members.doc: TwoSidedFoliage back-light bleed, 0..1

members.name: m_sheenIntensity
members.doc: Cloth sheen lobe strength, 0..1

members.name: m_eyeParams
members.doc: Eye: transported by record, never by a GBuffer lane

members.name: m_graphParamsExt
members.doc:
Lanes 4.. of a graph whose parameters outgrew the legacy four (see
MaterialGraph::FGraphParam). Empty for every material that fits, so the
per-frame proxy copy of such a material costs exactly what it did.

members.name: m_reflective
members.doc: forward transparent reflection opt-in

members.name: m_physicsMaterial
members.doc:
What the surface is made of once something collides with it. The path
names a `.physmat`, which is where friction, restitution and the
surface type are already authored together; the inline name is the
fallback for a material that only wants to say "this is metal".

The surface is held as a NAME rather than the enum because ESurfaceType
lives in Physics, well above the renderer in the module order — the same
reason it serializes by name everywhere else.

members.name: m_parent
members.doc: null = base material

members.name: m_overrideFlags
members.doc: Which properties are overridden (All = standalone material)

types.name: Material
types.doc:
An instance can inherit from a parent material and override only specific
properties.

Ownership: a Material is RefCounted and lives behind Ref<Material>. Assets
(ModelResource, MaterialAsset) hold the Ref; a component's raw `Material*`
is a VIEW derived from a Ref somebody else holds, never an owner. The last
Ref to drop frees the material and, through it, its GPU texture refs —
exactly once, however many components shared it. Creation goes through
Create()/CreatePBR()/Clone(): every allocation AND the deleting destructor
below run inside the Renderer image, so a Ref released from any other DLL
frees through the same heap that allocated.

members.name: Material
members.doc:
A material is never copied as a value: the count belongs to one object.
Clone() is the field-wise duplicate; CopyFrom() writes another material's
surface into THIS one without touching its identity or its count.

members.name: Clone
members.doc:
New object, same surface: textures are shared by Ref, the parent pointer
is shared, the identity is fresh — the DS cache treats it as a different
material, which it is.

members.name: CopyFrom
members.doc:
Overwrites the surface with `other`'s. Keeps this object's identity and
its in-flight transparent-write depth, and never lets the texture
version step backwards: the DS cache keys on it, and a version that
re-reached an old value would hand back the old descriptor set.

members.name: ResetInPlace
members.doc:
Back to a default-constructed surface IN PLACE — the object, its address
and its identity survive, so every Ref and every view keeps working.
This is the reimport contract: an asset reloads its material's contents,
it does not replace the material. The texture version moves forward for
the same reason CopyFrom's does.

members.name: GetStateVersion
members.doc:
Moves on every write to the surface (any setter, CopyFrom, ResetInPlace,
ResetToParent), including writes inside an FTransparentWriteScope. It
says nothing about the parent: a cache that snapshots an instance must
also check the parent chain.

members.name: GetAverageTextureColor
members.doc:
Linear-space average of the albedo texture (white when untextured
or the average is unknown). The GI voxelizer multiplies the flat base
color by this — matching the GBuffer's baseColor * texture composition
at 1-texel resolution — so GI bounce and SDF/RT reflections carry the
texture's actual tint instead of the bare base color.

members.name: GetAverageTextureAlpha
members.doc:
Linear average of the albedo texture's ALPHA channel (1 when
untextured/unknown). For alpha-masked materials this is the cutout
coverage — the GI voxelizer dithers occupancy by it and the RT ray
queries use it as the stochastic any-hit accept probability.

members.name: IsTransparent
members.doc:
Translucent when the surface lets anything through OR when its blend
mode is not plain alpha: a FULLY opaque additive material (glow cards,
holograms) still has to leave the GBuffer and draw in the blended pass,
and inferring translucency from opacity alone silently made those
opaque.

members.name: SetBlendMode
members.doc:
How a translucent surface combines with what is behind it. Alpha is
the historical (and default) behaviour; Additive adds light (fire,
glows), Modulate multiplies (stained glass, smoked plastic). The RHI
has carried all three since G5 — this is the material-level choice
that was missing, so authors could only ever get alpha.

members.name: SetAlphaMasked
members.doc:
Alpha-masked (cutout) rendering — foliage/fences: the GBuffer and
shadow passes clip pixels whose albedo alpha falls below the cutoff
instead of blending. Independent of IsTransparent (which routes to
the blended pass).

members.name: SetDoubleSided
members.doc: Double-sided: rendered with backface culling off (leaf cards, cloth).

members.name: SetSpecularColor
members.doc: Legacy specular properties (for backward compatibility)

members.name: SetAlbedoTex
members.doc:
Instance inheritance: a texture setter marks its override flag, and
the getter falls back to the parent when this instance hasn't overridden
the slot — so an instance with no texture override renders the parent's
texture instead of nothing. Base materials (no parent) always use local.

members.name: SetOpacityTex
members.doc:
Standalone opacity/cutout mask — the DCC-FBX foliage convention, where
coverage lives in its own grayscale map instead of the albedo's alpha.
When bound, the masked passes clip against THIS texture's red channel
rather than the albedo's alpha (an opaque albedo would clip nothing and
leave the card a solid quad). Unbound = clip against albedo alpha.

members.name: SetDetailAlbedoTex
members.doc:
Detail maps — overlaid on primary albedo / normal at close range. Used
to add high-frequency surface detail without 4K source textures.
detailTiling multiplies the UVs (typically 4-8x). The overlay strength
is gated by the mask map's B channel when a mask map is set, so the
detail can be limited to specific regions (e.g. dirt-mask only on the
bottom half of a wall).

members.name: SetMaskMapTex
members.doc:
Mask map — single RGBA8 replaces metallic + AO + smoothness + detail
mask, packed HDRP-style:
R = metallic, G = AO, B = detail mask, A = smoothness (1 - roughness)
When set, the shader uses the mask map values instead of the scalar
metallic/AO/roughness in BaseColor/PBRParams. Saves descriptor slots
and bandwidth vs separate textures.

members.name: SetHeightTex
members.doc:
Parallax Occlusion Mapping. Height map is a single-channel R8 texture
where 0 = surface, 1 = deepest point. The shader ray-marches along the
tangent-space view direction to find the intersection with the height
field and displaces UVs accordingly — adds genuine 3D-looking detail
at silhouettes without changing geometry.

heightScale ~0.02-0.08 for typical floor/wall textures. Larger values
exaggerate but break at grazing view angles ("swimming texels"). The
shader uses adaptive step count (8-32) based on view-angle perpendicular-
ness to keep grazing angles sharp without wasting samples head-on.

members.name: SetClearCoatIntensity
members.doc:
Clear coat — a second specular lobe on top of the base BRDF, modeling
a thin transparent lacquer layer (car paint, painted wood, soda cans).
Fixed F0 = 0.04 (IOR 1.5 lacquer), per-material intensity scalar
attenuates the lobe. Clear coat roughness is independent of base
roughness — a rough base under a glossy coat is the classic look.

Intensity 0 disables the lobe entirely; 1 = full strength. Typical
values: 0.6-0.9 for shiny car paint, 0.3-0.5 for satin lacquer.

members.name: SetAnisotropy
members.doc:
Anisotropy — stretches the specular highlight along the surface tangent
(positive) or bitangent (negative). The signature look for brushed
metal, hair, vinyl records, satin. Zero = isotropic (standard GGX).

The lighting pass derives the tangent direction from screen-space
position derivatives — no per-mesh tangent texture support yet, so the
anisotropy direction approximately follows the surface's screen-space
U/V flow. For authored brush direction, a future iteration would store
a tangent map in G-Buffer or sample it here.

members.name: SetSubsurfaceStrength
members.doc:
Subsurface scattering — fakes the warm glow on the shadow-side of skin /
wax / foliage by softening the diffuse terminator and tinting with
albedo. Strength 0 = standard Lambert; 1 = full wrap with curvature.
Not real Jimenez-style blur SSS — this is a Penner-style curvature
approximation that costs only a fwidth + a few mul-adds per pixel.

members.name: SetIridescenceIntensity
members.doc:
Iridescence — thin-film interference giving hue shifts based on view
angle. Approximated as an HSV rainbow swept by NdotV, mixed with the
standard Fresnel by `intensity`. 0 = disabled. Used for soap bubbles,
oil slicks, peacock feathers, beetle wings.

members.name: SetHair
members.doc:
Hair shading model — switches the lighting pass to an anisotropic
Kajiya-Kay strand model (dual shifted specular lobes) instead of GGX, for
hair/fur cards. Mutually exclusive with iridescence in the GBuffer pack
(the hair flag rides the sign of the iridescence lane). Pair with a
negative Anisotropy so the highlight stretches across the strand width.

members.name: SetShadingModel
members.doc:
Explicit shading model (G2). DefaultLit doubles as "legacy auto":
GetEffectiveShadingModel derives Hair/Subsurface from the older
per-scalar knobs so every existing asset keeps its look without a
resave. IDs are the GBuffer wire format (RT3.A high 3 bits) — 0 MUST
stay DefaultLit, because impostors and material-less draws write a
zero alpha and must remain plain-lit.

members.name: SetTransmissionStrength
members.doc:
TwoSidedFoliage transmission: how much light bleeds through the
surface from behind, tinted by albedo. Only sampled when the shading
model is TwoSidedFoliage (it is that model's custom GBuffer lane).

members.name: SetSheenIntensity
members.doc:
Cloth sheen: how much of the Charlie retro-reflective lobe rides on top
of the base diffuse. It is the Cloth model's custom lane, so it only
reaches the GBuffer when the material asks for that shading model.

members.name: SetEyeParams
members.doc:
Eye's parameters. They reach the shader through the frame's
surface-parameter record, not through a G-Buffer lane, so they are only
read when the effective shading model is Eye.

members.name: HasAnyTexture
members.doc:
Uses the fallback getters so an instance counts textures inherited from
its parent (not just its own overrides).

members.name: SetTerrainSplat
members.doc:
Terrain splat: the GBuffer draws this material through the
TERRAIN_SPLAT pipeline — vertex color = 4 layer weights over the
albedo/detailAlbedo/detailNormal/maskMap image slots.

members.name: SetFoliageWind
members.doc:
Foliage wind: the GBuffer draws this material through the FOLIAGE
pipeline — vertex color alpha = bend weight, DetailParams repurposed
as wind direction/strength/speed (foliage has no detail maps).

members.name: SetWindParams
members.signature: void SetWindParams(const Vec2& direction, float strength, float speed)

members.name: SetReflective
members.doc:
Reflective translucent surface: the forward transparent pass casts a
single mirror reflection ray through the world SDF clipmap (shaded from
the radiance cache, sky on miss) and composites it Fresnel-weighted over
the glass. Off by default — a non-reflective transparent keeps the plain
ambient+refraction look (bit-identical). High/Epic + the
r.Reflections.Translucent cvar gate it globally. Clear-coat transparents
draw a coat reflection from the same source regardless of this flag.

members.name: SetWater
members.doc:
Water: the transparent pass draws this material through the WATER
pipeline — Gerstner vertex displacement + fresnel shading. The material
must also be transparent (opacity < 1) to reach that pass at all.

members.name: SetWaterWaveParams
members.signature: void SetWaterWaveParams(const Vec2& direction, float amplitude, float wavelength, float steepness, float speed)

members.name: SetWorldGrid
members.doc:
World grid: the albedo becomes the procedural grid and the albedo
texture is ignored. MaterialOverride has no bit left, so an instance
inherits the grid from its parent unless it switches it on itself.

members.name: kWorldGridAlbedoLane
members.doc:
The GBuffer push block's bindless-albedo lane names a table slot when it
is >= 0 and the per-material set at -1; this value below both selects
the grid, so no pipeline or push-constant byte had to be added for it.

members.name: PackWorldGridDetailParams
members.doc:
DetailParams of a grid draw: x = major cell, y = minor cell (metres,
clamped away from zero), z/w = major/minor line shades.

members.name: SetPhysicsMaterialPath
members.doc:
The physics surface. Empty on an instance means "whatever the parent
says": MaterialOverride has no bit left to spend on this, and an
instance that wanted to differ physically authors one of these fields.

members.name: HasAuthoredPhysics
members.doc:
Whether anyone authored a physics answer at all. A material that did not
has to leave the collider exactly as it was, which is what keeps every
scene predating this block behaving identically.

members.name: CreateInstance
members.doc:
The instance points at its parent but does not own it: whoever holds
the parent's Ref (its asset) must outlive the instance, as before.

members.name: CreateMetallic
members.signature: static Ref<Material> CreateMetallic(const Vec4& baseColor, float shininess = 64.0f)

members.name: CreatePBR
members.signature: static Ref<Material> CreatePBR(const Vec4& baseColor, float metallic, float roughness, float ao = 1.0f)

members.name: CreatePBRMetal
members.signature: static Ref<Material> CreatePBRMetal(const Vec4& baseColor, float roughness = 0.3f)

members.name: CreatePBRDielectric
members.signature: static Ref<Material> CreatePBRDielectric(const Vec4& baseColor, float roughness = 0.5f)

members.name: CreateWorldGrid
members.doc:
The engine default surface: a mid-grey world grid, rough dielectric.
Every mesh that has no material of its own draws with this.

members.name: SetGraphShaderId
members.doc:
Compiled material graph (UE5-gap Q1). A non-empty id names the
per-material GBuffer permutation in the shader archive
("Materials/<hex>"); GraphTextures carries the graph's slot-ordered
texture bindings for the material descriptor set. Empty id = the
classic uber-shader path, untouched.

members.name: GetGraphShaderHash
members.doc:
The id as the number it was printed from, so the renderer's ten graph
pipeline caches key on a word instead of rebuilding a 16-character
string per draw per pass per cascade — one character past MSVC's small
string buffer, so every one of those copies allocated.

members.name: HashGraphShaderId
members.doc:
The canonical id is "%016llx" of the graph's content hash, so parsing it
recovers that hash exactly and adds no collision the hash did not
already carry. Anything else — a hand-written id in a test — is folded
instead, which keeps it distinct without pretending it round-trips.

members.name: SetGraphHasWpo
members.doc:
G4: whether the graph links a World Position Offset. Drives the
shadow/velocity pipeline swaps — a no-WPO graph keeps the cheap uber
vertex path there (the pixel splice is independent of this flag).

members.name: SetGraphWpoBound
members.doc:
Conservative world-space bound on |WPO| from the graph compile (0 = no
WPO; a huge sentinel = unboundable subtree). The meshlet path inflates
its per-cluster cull spheres by it — or, at the sentinel, stops
trusting geometric kills for the draw entirely.

members.name: SetSubstrateTop
members.doc:
The graph's Substrate slab folded to one packed G-Buffer word, 0 when the
material has no slab or when its slab moves per pixel. Read by the paths
that cache ONE answer per surface and therefore cannot carry a per-pixel
coat: the GI surface cache's card capture and the ray-traced hit shading.
Everything that shades per pixel reads the slab out of the G-Buffer and
must ignore this.

members.name: SetGraphParamLane
members.signature: void SetGraphParamLane(uint32_t lane, const Vec4& v)
members.doc:
R4: the runtime parameter lanes the graph pipelines push per draw.
MaterialAsset seeds the graph's defaults and maps names to lanes;
gameplay writes lanes through it (SetScalarParameter/SetVectorParameter).
The first four lanes are the legacy block every graph pipeline reads;
a graph that needs more sizes the extension once at GPU-create time
(SetGraphParamLaneCount, from CompiledShader::paramLanes) and the
upload copies GetGraphParamLaneCount() lanes instead of four.

types.name: Material::FTransparentWriteScope
types.doc:
Writes that REPRODUCE a material rather than author it — the .mat
loader replaying a saved document, the graph compiler folding its result
onto the flat fields, a GPU re-resolve rebinding textures — must not read
as user edits. Inside this scope the setters still write their fields but
stop raising override bits, so an instance keeps inheriting exactly what
its stored mask says it inherits instead of freezing at whatever its
parent happened to hold the last time the file was opened.

types.name: FMaterialRenderProxy
types.doc:
Render-thread snapshot of a Material (+ its resolved parent chain), the
UE5 FMaterialRenderProxy analog. The game thread builds one per frame; the
render thread reads only this copy, never the live Material. Ref-counted so
the frame packet keeps it alive past the game thread freeing the source.

members.name: sourceKey
members.doc: original Material's stable id — DS-cache key across frames (0 = no material)

types.name: FMaterialRenderProxyCache
types.doc:
The game-thread owner of every FMaterialRenderProxy. A proxy is immutable
once built, so last frame's snapshot is handed out again for as long as the
source material's (identity, state version) and its parent's proxy are
unchanged — in a frame where nobody edited a material, nothing is copied.
Several in-flight frame packets may hold the same proxy; that is safe only
because nothing writes to a proxy after Get returns it.

members.name: BeginFrame
members.doc: Opens a packet: forgets the per-packet dedup map, keeps the snapshots.

members.name: Get
members.doc:
The snapshot of `material` for this packet; the same Ref for every call
with the same material inside one packet.

members.name: EndFrame
members.doc:
Drops snapshots no packet asked for in kIdleFrames. Keyed by address,
so an entry outliving its material is harmless (the identity check
refuses it), but it pins that material's textures until it ages out.

members.name: SetReuseEnabled
members.doc:
Off = snapshot every material every packet, the behaviour before the
state version existed. Kept for A/B and as the escape hatch if a writer
that bypasses the setters ever turns up.

types.name: GpuMeshlet
types.doc:
One cluster of a static mesh (virtualized-geometry path): ≤64
vertices / ≤124 triangles indexing into the shared per-mesh remap +
packed-triangle arrays below. Layout matches the HLSL StructuredBuffer
element in the mesh-shading path byte-for-byte (96 bytes) — keep both
in lockstep.

Stage-2 cluster DAG: selfSphere/selfError describe the group that
PRODUCED this meshlet by simplification (leaves: own bounds, error 0);
parentSphere/parentError describe the group this meshlet belongs to as
a child (the group whose simplification replaces it one level up).
Children of a group and the parents produced from it carry the SAME
sphere+error bits, so the task shader's cut test evaluates to exact
complements — a group's children and parents can never both render.
Defaults reproduce stage-1 behavior (always drawn when the cut is
evaluated): selfError 0, parentError infinite, level 0.

types.name: MeshletData
types.doc:
CPU-side meshlet set for one mesh, built at import (Game's
FMeshletBuild). vertexIndices remaps meshlet-local vertex slots to the
mesh vertex buffer; triangles packs one triangle per uint32
(i0 | i1<<8 | i2<<16, meshlet-local 8-bit indices). Meshlets are
ordered by DAG level, level 0 (leaves) first.

free.name: kMeshletErrorInfinity
free.doc:
Sentinel for "no coarser representation exists" (DAG root). Kept well
below FLT_MAX so shader-side scale multiplies can't overflow to inf.

free.signature: static_assert(sizeof(GpuMeshlet) == 96, "GpuMeshlet must stay 96 bytes (HLSL MeshletEntry mirror)")

types.name: FMeshletFallbackRun
types.doc:
One batched material run as the meshlet compute fallback reads it
(GBuffer/MeshletFallbackCull.comp.hlsl, MeshletFallbackRun): where its task
groups sit in the batch's group list, and the slice of the shared triangle
list its survivors append into.

members.name: ObjectReach
members.doc:
Height-map displacement reach in object units (scaled by the draw's
largest axis in the cull) and the graph's World Position Offset bound in
world units: both grow the cull sphere, as in the task stage.

types.name: FMeshletFallback
types.doc:
The layout both halves of the fallback agree on: the argument buffer's
header and per-run stride (one indexed-indirect command a run), the
triangle budget the list and its identity index buffer are sized to, and
how the runs share it. Pure, so the headless meshlet row pins it.

members.name: kRunNoCone
members.doc:
The import-built backface cone no longer describes displaced or
WPO-moved normals.

members.name: kRunFinestLevel
members.doc:
Displacement draws the finest DAG level only: the simplifier never saw
the height map, so a coarse level has nothing left to displace.

members.name: kRunNoFrustum
members.doc: An unboundable WPO subtree: no radius is safe, so no frustum kill.

members.name: kTriangleBudget
members.doc:
One uint a triangle in the list, three identity indices a triangle, two
uints a surviving cluster: 4 + 12 + 8 MB at a million triangles.

members.name: DisplacementReach
members.signature: static float DisplacementReach(float magnitude, float center)
members.doc:
How far the height map can move a vertex along its normal, in object
units: height 0 is the surface and 1 the deepest point, so the centre
splits the magnitude between rising and sinking.

members.name: RunFlags
members.signature: static uint32_t RunFlags(bool twoSided, float displacementMagnitude, float wpoBound)
members.doc:
The cull flags of a run; `wpoBound` at or past 1e30 is the graph
compiler's unboundable sentinel.

members.name: AssignSlices
members.signature: static uint32_t AssignSlices(const std::vector<uint32_t>& needs, uint32_t budget, std::vector<uint32_t>& outBase, std::vector<uint32_t>& outCapacity)
members.doc:
Lays the runs' slices end to end in the budget. A run asks for the
triangles its finest level would draw — the DAG cut never draws more —
and gets that while room lasts; past the budget a run is clipped, and a
run that finds none left gets an empty slice. Returns the triangles

types.name: FMeshletPackedVertex
types.doc:
The meshlet pool's vertex stream, quantized against its page's own bounds.
Mirrors MeshletVertexPacked in Shaders/Private/GBuffer/MeshletVertex.hlsli:

w[0]     position x | position y   16 bits each, against the page AABB
w[1]     position z | sign bit     bit 16 = bitangent handedness < 0
w[2]     normal, octahedral 16+16
w[3]     tangent, octahedral 16+16
w[4]     texCoord  u | v           16 bits each, against the page UV range
w[5]     texCoord1 u | v
w[6..9]  colour, four untouched float32

40 B against LitVertex's 72. Per-page residency duplicates a vertex into
every page that references it, and this is what pays that duplication back:
the bounds are per page, so 16 bits cover a small box rather than the model.

specification to mirror. The meshlet GBuffer row's MRT comparison against the
classic pipeline is what proves the two halves still agree on a real GPU.

types.name: FMeshletPage
types.doc:
One streaming page: a contiguous run of clusters in the page-ordered
cluster array, closed over cluster groups (a group's members never
straddle a page — evicting half a group would leave the fine side of that
boundary partly drawn, which is exactly a crack) and over DAG levels.
Pages run fine -> coarse and residency is always a SUFFIX of them, which
is what makes ancestor-closure structural: a cluster's DAG parents live at
a strictly coarser level, hence in a strictly later page, so a resident
cluster's ancestors are resident by construction.

maxParentError is a PREFIX max over pages 0..this one, object space: the
screen-error budget test that decides eviction is therefore monotone and a
single scan finds the floor.

firstPageVertex/pageVertexCount name the page's own vertex slice: the
DISTINCT source vertices its clusters reference, deduplicated inside the
page and duplicated across pages. Nothing else makes a page independently
releasable — coarse DAG levels re-index the same source vertices as the
leaves, so a shared per-mesh vertex block can only be freed when the whole
mesh goes, which is exactly the memory paging was supposed to reclaim.

The slice the pool ALLOCATES is kBoundsSlots larger than pageVertexCount:
the page's dequantization bounds sit in the slots ahead of its vertices, and
remapCount carries kRemapHeaderWords extra words per cluster naming that
slot. Both are page-relative, so a page that comes back at a different pool
offset still needs nothing rewritten but its own remap words.
firstRemap and remapCount deliberately do NOT measure the same stream.
firstRemap indexes `localRemap`, which holds one word per cluster VERTEX
slot and nothing else; remapCount is what the page ALLOCATES, which on a
quantized page also carries kRemapHeaderWords per cluster for the bounds
slot. Collapsing them would either put header words into localRemap (which
is parallel to the import's vertexIndices) or under-allocate the page.

types.name: FMeshletPageLayout
types.doc:
Page-ordered view of one mesh's cluster DAG. `order` maps a page-ordered
slot to its index in the source MeshletData; the source is never mutated.
`groupPage` gives, per cluster-group id, the page holding that group's
MEMBERS — the value the descent gate consults when deciding whether a
coarser cluster may stand in for children that paged out.

`pageVertices` concatenates every page's distinct SOURCE vertex indices
(slice [firstPageVertex, +pageVertexCount)); `localRemap` is parallel to the
page-ordered remap stream and gives, per cluster vertex slot, that vertex's
index WITHIN its page's slice. Both are page-relative on purpose: the pool
offset a page lands at changes on every page-in, and a remap word rebuilt as
pageVertexOffset + localRemap survives the move where a stored absolute
index could not.

types.name: FMeshletSwRasterCluster
types.doc:
One cluster handed from the meshlet task stage to the software rasterizer,
mirroring `SwRasterCluster` in Shaders/Private/GBuffer/MeshletSwRaster.hlsli. The
model transform is copied rather than referenced because the raster dispatch
carries no push constant of the draw that produced the cluster, and an
instanced dispatch's rows come from the transform pool rather than from the
draw's own matrix. Only the three affine rows are stored; the fourth is
implicit, which is what keeps the record at 64 B.

members.name: SurfaceRecord
members.doc:
The owning INSTANCE's surface-parameter record index, stamped by the task
stage. It has to live here rather than in the resolve's per-material
table: that table is keyed by material, so one entry would hand every
draw and every instance of a material the same record. 0xFFFF is the
no-record sentinel (FSurfaceCode::NoRecord, which this tier cannot
include). This was the padding word — the record is still 64 B.

admission path the GPUMesh overload takes, minus the vertex copy.

members.name: RequestSkinned
members.signature: Alloc RequestSkinned(const void* key, const MeshletData& data)
members.doc:
Skinned residency: admits the cluster DAG (meshlets/remap/triangles)
with no vertex copy and 0-based remap. The mesh-shading path feeds the
live vertices from a per-instance pre-skin buffer and refits the cluster
bounds each frame, so the pool holds only the topology.

members.name: NoteScreenErrorBudget
members.signature: void NoteScreenErrorBudget(const void* key, float budget, uint64_t frame)
members.doc:
A mesh is resident as a suffix of its pages: pages [floor, count) hold
GPU vertex/remap/triangle storage and are the only ones the draw
dispatches (Alloc.meshletBase/meshletCount describe exactly that suffix,
so every consumer of an Alloc — GBuffer, shadow casters, the skinned
refit — respects residency with no change of its own). All three arrays
are allocated when a page is granted and released when it is evicted;
nothing durable stores an absolute pool index, so a page that returns to
a different offset is simply re-emitted against its new one.

The floor tracks the cut, it does not lead it: a page is evictable only
once every cluster in it provably FAILS the task stage's parent gate,
i.e. the cut has already stopped selecting those clusters. Advancing
the floor is then a no-op on the visible set, which is why the
transition needs no double-buffering.

Callers publish what the cull wants as a screen-error budget: the
object-space error a cluster group may carry and still be replaced by
its parent at this draw's distance,
budget = threshold * distance / (scale * projScale)
with `threshold`/`projScale` the same pair the task stage's LodParams
carry and `distance` the NEAREST point of the draw's bounding sphere
(conservative: every cluster's own gate sees a distance at least this
large). Budget 0 pins the mesh whole. The minimum over a frame's draws
wins; a mesh that WAS being noted and stops parks at its coarsest
pages, while a key that was never noted at all stays whole — a caller
that does not publish what its cull wants gets no guess made for it.

members.name: EvictablePageFloor
members.signature: static uint32_t EvictablePageFloor(const FMeshletPageLayout& layout, float budget, float margin)
members.doc:
Pages evictable/keepable at that budget — the hysteresis band. Eviction
waits for kPageEvictMargin headroom, page-in fires the moment the
budget stops covering a page, so a mesh crossing the boundary does not
thrash.

members.name: BuildPageLayout
members.signature: static void BuildPageLayout(const MeshletData& data, uint32_t pageBudgetBytes, FMeshletPageLayout& out, bool quantized = true)
members.doc:

assert group closure / root pinning / ancestor closure without a device.

`quantized` says whether the pages will hold packed pool vertices — it
prices a page's remap slice with the per-cluster bounds header word and
its vertices at the packed stride. A skinned entry passes false: its live
vertices come from a per-instance pre-skin buffer, its remap indexes that
buffer directly, and a header word there would shift every index.

types.doc:
The auto-exposure decision, stated once on the CPU. AutoExposureAverage.comp.hlsl
mirrors these functions step for step — the same relationship LidarTrace.comp.hlsl
has with FLidarPattern — because the interesting failures here are not "the
dispatch did not run" but "the floor was in the wrong units" and "the
percentile window picked the black bin", and neither is visible in a
screenshot. Keeping the arithmetic in a pure function is what makes those
testable at all.

members.signature: static float MeanBin(const uint32_t* bins, uint32_t binCount)
members.doc:
Mean of the metered histogram, in bin units. Bin 0 is the black/unmetered
bin and never contributes: a large dark region would otherwise drag the
average down and the adaptation would answer by brightening the room.

members.name: PercentileBin
members.signature: static float PercentileBin(const uint32_t* bins, uint32_t binCount, float lowPercent, float highPercent)
members.doc:

are clipped rather than included whole, so the result moves continuously
as the histogram shifts — a bin flipping in or out wholesale is a visible
exposure step.

members.name: ResolveBin
members.signature: static float ResolveBin(const uint32_t* bins, uint32_t binCount, int meteringMode, float lowPercent, float highPercent)
members.doc:

the mean of what was deposited".

members.signature: static float LuminanceFromBin(float bin, float minLogLum, float logLumRange)

members.name: TargetExposure
members.signature: static float TargetExposure(float averageLuminance, float keyValue, float evCompensation, float minEV, float maxEV)
members.doc:
The clamp the whole item is about. minEV/maxEV are stops; the pair is
ordered here rather than trusted, because an artist who drags the floor
above the ceiling should get a pinned exposure, not an inverted clamp
that returns the ceiling.

members.name: RebasePrevious
members.signature: static float RebasePrevious(float previous, float preExposureRatio)
members.doc:
The stored exposure is a RESIDUAL on top of pre-exposure: what the
tonemap multiplies after pre-exposure has already scaled the HDR. So the
value carried over from last frame is expressed in last frame's
pre-exposure, while this frame's target — and the authored clamps, which
are already divided by it — are expressed in this frame's. Blending the
two without rebasing mixes two scales.

It is invisible whenever the controller is still, because the ratio is
then 1, and that is exactly when the pumping it causes cannot be seen.
With a doubling pre-exposure and a genuinely static scene the rebased
previous equals the target, so the blend is a no-op and the image holds
— which is the whole point.

members.name: Adapt
members.signature: static float Adapt(float previous, float target, float deltaSeconds, float speedUp, float speedDown)
members.doc:
Frame-rate-independent exponential approach. A non-positive previous
value is the first frame after a reset — snapping there avoids a visible
fade up from black every time the target is recreated.

members.name: tonemapOperator
members.doc:
0 = ACES (Narkowicz fit), 1 = AgX, 2 = Reinhard, 3 = clamp,
4 = ACES RRT + ODT (the reference output transform, sRGB 100-nit ODT on
an SDR display, the 1000-nit ODT under HDR output),
5 = display LUT (displayLutPath replaces the tone curve; ACES RRT + ODT
while none is loaded).

members.name: physicalCameraEnabled
members.doc:
Physical camera (R22). When enabled, `exposure` above is IGNORED and the
scene is exposed from the three numbers a cinematographer actually sets:
f-stop, shutter time and ISO. The point is not a different look — it is
that "f/2.8, 1/50, ISO 400" is a specification a DP can hand over and a
lighting artist can match, while a bare multiplier of 1.8 is not.

exposure = 1 / (1.2 * 2^EV100), EV100 = log2(N^2 / t) - log2(ISO / 100)
— the saturation-based speed convention, so one stop of aperture, one
stop of shutter and one stop of ISO all move the image by exactly the
same amount, which is the property that makes the units worth having.

members.doc: N

members.doc:
The ONE place the exposure multiplier is decided. Three consumers read
it (tonemap, the bloom bright-pass, pre-exposure) and they must agree;
computing it at each of them is how a physical camera ends up applied to
the image but not to the bloom threshold.

members.doc: Post-AA contrast-adaptive sharpening (0 = off)

members.name: autoExposureMetering
members.doc:
Auto-exposure metering: 0=average, 1=spot, 2=center-weighted,
3=histogram percentile; EV compensation shifts the adaptation target by
2^EV stops.

members.name: autoExposureMinEV
members.doc:
The floor and ceiling of the adapted exposure, in stops (multiplier =
2^EV). These were hardcoded at 0.05 and 16.0, which is why a scene lit
for a dark room came out grey: with nothing bright in frame the
adaptation ran into the 16× ceiling and lifted the blacks until the room
read as fog. A horror scene wants that ceiling brought down — the dark
has to stay dark — so the pair is authored per scene rather than fixed.
The defaults are exactly the old constants, so an existing scene that
does not touch them is unchanged.

members.name: autoExposureSpeedUp
members.doc:
Adaptation rates in 1/s, asymmetric like the eye: the target falling
(scene got brighter) is followed at SpeedUp, the target rising (scene
got darker) at SpeedDown. Dark adaptation is the slow one, and how slow
it is *is* the pacing of a scanner sweep revealing a room.

members.name: autoExposureLowPercent
members.doc:
Percentile metering window, in percent of the metered pixels ordered by
luminance. Only read when autoExposureMetering == 3. Ignoring the
darkest `low` and the brightest `1 - high` is what stops one lamp or one
pool of black from deciding the whole frame's exposure — a spatial
weight cannot do that, because the offending pixels are anywhere.

members.name: bloomEnabled
members.doc:
Bloom. The bright pass runs on EXPOSED radiance, so bloomThreshold and
bloomClamp are in display-white units (1.0 = white) and mean the same
thing in every scene. bloomIntensity is a BLEND weight, not a gain:
final = lerp(scene, bloom, bloomIntensity) — the fraction of the pixel
the lens scattered. bloomClamp bounds how much exposed luminance one
bright area may push into its neighbours (0 = unbounded).

members.name: ssrEnabled
members.doc:
On like UE's post-process defaults; the tier still decides whether SSR
runs at all (r.SSR, Low hard-off). Off here meant an empty post volume
switched SSR off on every tier, so High measured 0.000 ms.

members.name: tint
members.doc:

types.name: FLightChannels
types.doc:
Per-pixel light channels. The G-Buffer had no free channel, so the mask rides
the LOW NIBBLE of RT3.B — the lane that used to carry 8-bit bias-encoded
anisotropy alone. Anisotropy keeps the HIGH nibble under a signed code whose
midpoint (8) decodes to exactly 0, so every material that authors no
anisotropy writes the same neutral value it always did.

RT3.B byte = (anisoNibble << 4) | (lightChannels & 0xF)

4 channels ship (UE5 exposes 3). A surface mask of 0 means "all channels", so
any G-Buffer writer that never fills the nibble (foliage impostors, decals
preserving the destination) stays fully lit.

Anisotropy nibble 0 is a sentinel, not a lobe: the signed code never
produces it (the most negative byte lands on 1), so it is free to mean "this
surface does not receive shadows" — the mesh's Receive Shadows toggle had no
other lane left in the G-Buffer. A surface that opts out of shadows reads
back as isotropic; that is the trade, and it costs nothing on any pixel that
was already being written. The draw-side transport is the GBuffer push
constant's MaskParams.y, where bit 4 above the channel nibble carries the
opt-out so every writer that packs RT3.B (classic, meshlet, SW resolve)
sees the same value.

Every method below is the exact mirror of the HLSL in GBufferFill.hlsl /
DeferredLighting.hlsl — the headless light-channels test pins them together.

types.name: FGBufferMaterialRecord
types.doc:
PBRParams.z carries a packed uint32:
bits  0..6  : texture flags  (one bit each — see list below)
bits  7..14 : clearCoatIntensity  (8-bit fixed point, /255 → 0..1)
bits 15..22 : clearCoatRoughness  (8-bit fixed point, /255 → 0..1)
bits 23..30 : anisotropy          (8-bit signed, encoded (v+1)*127.5 → maps [-1..1] → [0..255])
bit  31     : reserved

textureFlags bit layout (bits 0..6 of PBRParams.z):
0: hasAlbedoTex
1: hasNormalTex
2: hasMetallicRoughnessTex (legacy combined RG)
3: hasDetailAlbedoTex
4: hasDetailNormalTex
5: hasMaskMap            (R=metallic, G=AO, B=detailMask, A=smoothness)
6: hasHeightMap          (parallax occlusion mapping)

8-bit precision for clear coat / anisotropy is ~0.4% per step — well
below the threshold of visual quantisation for those parameters.

DetailParams:
xy : UV tiling multiplier for both detail albedo + detail normal
z  : detailAlbedoStrength (0..1) — blend amount over primary albedo
w  : detailNormalStrength (0..1) — strength of detail normal influence

These seven lanes are one draw's MATERIAL RECORD, uploaded per frame into the
MaterialGraphParams buffer (set 0 binding 9, behind the graph-material
entries) and deduplicated by content; the push block below carries only the
record's index and the lanes that change per draw. Vulkan guarantees 128
bytes of push constants and Intel ANV / AMDVLK report exactly that — the old
176-byte block (Model + these lanes) made the G-Buffer pipeline itself
uncreatable there. GBufferFill.hlsl's MowoLoadGBufferDraw is the mirror.
The .w lanes of ExtendedParams, BindlessSlots and MaskParams are per draw:
a record's copies are ignored and the push block's are used.

types.name: MeshletGBufferPushConstants
types.doc:
Meshlet GBuffer variant: the shared block plus the task-stage cull tail —
matches the MESHLET_CULL_PC extension in GBufferFill.hlsl. VisBase = this
draw's slot base into the meshlet visibility buffer; CullFlags bit0 = Hi-Z
occlusion + two-phase visibility active, bit1 = phase-2 recovery pass,
bit2 = LOD-cut conflict tracking (tests only: drawn meshlets InterlockedOr
their child-group id with 1 and their producedBy group with 2 into the
visibility buffer — a slot reaching 3 proves a parent+child double render);
PyramidBase/Levels describe the GPU cull Hi-Z pyramid (level-0 width,
level count). The graph-material entry index rides the material record's
MaskParams.z lane, same as the classic graph pipelines. CullFlags bit 31
(displacement) also zeroes the record's parallax scale in the shader, since
the record is shared with the material's undisplaced draws.

LodParams drives the stage-2 cluster-DAG cut: x = screen-space error
threshold in pixels (r.MeshletLodError), y = projection scale
(0.5 * renderHeight * Proj[1][1]; <= 0 disables the error cut and
draws level-0 leaves only — the safe zero-init default), z = forced
DAG level (r.MeshletForceLod, < 0 = error-driven), w = the instanced
group's base row in the transform pool (the dispatch row is added to
it, so the ordinal doubles as the surface-record offset). Every
pipeline built from GBufferFillMeshlet must declare and push this
widened block.

each frame by the pre-skin + bounds-refit compute passes.

types.name: FPushAffineRows
types.doc:
Vulkan guarantees only 128 bytes of push constants and Intel ANV and AMDVLK
report exactly that, so a pipeline whose push range is larger fails to
create there. An AFFINE matrix (model transforms, an ortho cascade's light
view-projection) therefore travels as its first three rows; the shader
rebuilds row 3 as (0,0,0,1), which is bit-exact for every such matrix.

types.name: ShadowMeshletPushConstants
types.doc:
Depth-only meshlet caster (ShadowDepthMeshlet.mesh.hlsl). Model + the
cascade's LightViewProj ride the push so the mesh-shading shadow path needs
no per-cascade UBO; the task stage runs the cluster-DAG cut and frustum-culls
each survivor against LightViewProj, the mesh stage emits position only.
MeshletBase/Count point into the shared pool. Both matrices are affine (the
cascade projection is orthographic) and travel as FPushAffineRows.

LodParams is the cascade's own cut, not the camera's: x = allowed projected
error in SHADOW TEXELS, y = texels per world unit for this cascade
(0.5 * tileSize * its ortho scale; <= 0 keeps level-0 leaves only, the safe
zero-init default), z = forced DAG level (< 0 = error-driven), w = pad. A
cascade's projection is orthographic, so unlike the camera's cut the error
does not fall off with distance — MeshletCut.hlsli carries the reasoning.
StatsBase = this cascade's 16-counter block in the shadow stats buffer.

types.name: ShadowMeshletSkinnedPushConstants
types.doc:
Skinned twin: adds the per-instance pre-skin vertex buffer + refit-bounds
device addresses (the same buffers the GBuffer skinned meshlet path builds).
The two addresses leave 16 bytes for five cut scalars, so two pairs share a
lane: StatsBase rides the top byte above a 24-bit MeshletCount (a cascade
block starts at most at 3 * 16), and a forced DAG level L travels as
LodScale = -(L + 1). A forced level is tested before the scale, and a real
scale is never negative, so the shader recovers every field exactly.

types.name: FSceneViewFeatures
types.doc:
Per-view render feature mask.

A SceneRenderer can hold several views (the editor's quad layout renders
four of them live in one frame). Every view runs the same deferred core —
GBuffer, deferred lighting, tonemap, final blit — because that core is what
produces an image at all; everything above it is opt-in per view through
this mask.

The mask is honoured at the PASS level, not by silently lowering quality
inside a pass: a feature that is off means its passes never record, so the
cost is gone and the result is honest (an ortho reference pane genuinely
has no ambient occlusion rather than a cheaper approximation of it).
Per-view resources are still allocated for every view — the unified frame
graph imports them unconditionally — so the mask buys GPU time, and the
per-view render scale buys VRAM.

types.name: FSkinnedPoseBounds
types.doc:
A conservative world bound for a posed skinned mesh, and a hash of the pose.
A skinned vertex is a weighted blend of its bones' skinning matrices applied
to its bind-pose position, so it lies inside the convex hull of those
matrices applied to it — and therefore inside the union of every bone's
image of the bind-pose box. Without a bound, a skinned caster had to be
treated as reaching everything: it dirtied every page of every local
virtual shadow map each frame and was drawn into all of them. Dual
quaternion blending and morph targets can step slightly outside the matrix
hull, which the margin covers.

atlas with a page-table indirection texture — the texture analog of the VSM
page machinery. The cache owns the atlas (one big Image2D of tileStride²
tiles, where tileStride = pageSize + 2*border) and the page table (R32UI,
one texel per virtual page: 0xFFFFFFFF = non-resident, else slotY<<16 |
slotX). Borders replicate the neighbouring texels so bilinear sampling never
bleeds across a page seam. Pages are streamed from a provider: the GPU
feedback pass records which virtual pages a frame wants, the host decodes the
unique requests and pulls them through the provider a budget at a time. A
full atlas evicts the least-recently used page.

The cache is a mip pyramid: mip 0 is virtualPagesX × virtualPagesY pages,
each coarser mip halves both page counts down to a single 1×1 top mip. A
page at mip m still occupies one pageSize² atlas slot but covers 2^m× the
virtual-texel span, so its provider fill is a box-filtered downsample of the
source. The page table for every mip is packed into one R32UI image (all
mips share the mip-0 width; mip m's rows start at PageTableRowOffset(m)),
residency is keyed on (mip, pageX, pageY), and the shader falls back to a
resident coarser mip whenever the fine page it wants is not yet streamed —
so an unstreamed page reads a blurrier ancestor rather than black.

members.name: PageProvider
members.signature: using PageProvider = std::function<void(uint32_t mip, uint32_t pageX, uint32_t pageY, std::vector<uint8_t>& outPixels)>
members.doc:
Fills outPixels with tileStride² tightly-packed texels for one page of
the given mip — the inner pageSize² plus the border ring, box-filtered
over the page's 2^mip-scaled virtual-texel span. With border == 0 this is
exactly the inner page. For a block-compressed spec.format the bytes are
the tile's 4x4 blocks, row by row (FVirtualTextureTileFile's disk
provider hands them over as cooked), and tileStride must be a multiple
of 4 — Create refuses otherwise.
